question.text: Which of the following mutual fund transactions does NOT trigger a capital gains tax event?

answer.text: Switching from Growth option to IDCW option within the same scheme
Redemption of units through a Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP)
Transfer of mutual fund units to a spouse under a gift deed (transfer between specified relatives)
Transfer of units from one scheme to another under a Systematic Transfer Plan (STP)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Income Tax Act, 1961, gifts of capital assets (including mutual fund units) between specified relatives such as spouses are generally not regarded as a 'transfer' that triggers capital gains tax at the time of the gift. The recipient inherits the donor's cost of acquisition and holding period, and tax is determined when the recipient eventually redeems the units. The other listed transactions are taxable events: switching between scheme options is treated as redemption plus fresh purchase, SWP involves actual unit redemptions, and STP involves redemption from the source scheme. The Trap: All distractors are taxable mutual-fund events. Only a gift transfer to a specified relative escapes the capital-gains trigger at the time of transfer. Note: The cited NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook supports the taxability of SWP, STP and switch transactions but does not, in the pages reviewed, explicitly cover the spouse-gift / Section 47 exemption. The framing above reflects general Income Tax Act treatment of gifts to specified relatives rather than a direct workbook citation.
